form.applyNow: Changes apply immediately — no restart needed.

server.title: Server
server.countryHint: Used for titles' age ratings, profiles' age limits and Discover's Coming to cinemas list.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Posters, summaries, ratings, cast and episode titles.
metadata.tmdbKeyHint: Movies, collections and Fix Match use TMDB. Free key from themoviedb.org/settings/api. Without one, movies keep their file names and local artwork, or what their NFO files say.
metadata.tvShowsHint: Automatic uses TMDB when it has a key, then TheTVDB when it has one, else TVmaze, which needs none. Changing the source fetches every show again.
metadata.tvdbKeyHint: Only needed to use TheTVDB for TV shows. Get one at thetvdb.com/api-information.
metadata.tvdbPinHint: User-supported keys also need your subscriber PIN. Leave empty for other keys.
metadata.musicHint: Genres and release dates from MusicBrainz, and covers from the Cover Art Archive for albums that have none. Tags in the files win. No key needed; the first look-up takes about a second per album.
metadata.nfoHint: The NFO files Kodi, Jellyfin, Radarr and Sonarr keep next to movies and shows: their ids decide the match, and their details win over the metadata source's. Your edits win over them. Pley never changes them.
metadata.languageHint: For TMDB and TheTVDB. TVmaze is in English.
metadata.attribution: This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB. TV metadata from <tvdb>TheTVDB</tvdb>. TV data from TVmaze is licensed <license>CC BY-SA</license>; music data from MusicBrainz is public domain.

subtitles.title: Subtitles
subtitles.description: Find subtitles for a movie or episode on OpenSubtitles, from the player's subtitle menu.
subtitles.keyHint: Each server needs its own key: create a consumer at opensubtitles.com/consumers. Without one, subtitle search is off.
subtitles.accountHint: Optional. Downloads count against this account's daily quota instead of the key's smaller one.

scanning.title: Library scanning
scanning.watchHint: Pick up new, changed and deleted files automatically.
scanning.markersHint: Compare the audio of episodes in the background to offer Skip Intro and Skip Credits. Chapters named Intro or Credits are always used.
scanning.noChromaprint: This FFmpeg lacks Chromaprint, so only chapters can mark intros and credits.
scanning.seekPreviewsHint: Make the thumbnails shown above the seek bar, in the background, the first time a movie or episode is opened.
scanning.wholeLibrariesHint: After each scan, make missing seek previews and chapter pictures.
scanning.intervalHint: Minutes between full scans. 0 disables periodic scans.

libraryWork.label: When library work runs
libraryWork.hint: Finding intros and credits, and previews for whole libraries. They always wait while something plays; what someone opens or is watching goes first, at any hour.
libraryWork.needs: Needs Detect intros and credits, or Previews for whole libraries.
libraryWork.autoNote: Shows people are watching, titles on their lists and what's new go first, at any hour. The rest waits for the hours people rarely watch, which the server learns.
libraryWork.learned: Learned from what played over the last weeks, recent ones counting most, in the server's time.
libraryWork.learning: Still learning: until about a week of playback is known, the rest of the libraries goes on whenever nothing plays.
libraryWork.waitForOthersHint: Library work waits while other programs keep more of the processors busy than this.

signIn.title: Sign-in
signIn.requireTwoStepHint: Everyone with a password signs in with a code from an authenticator app. Whoever hasn't set it up does so at their next sign-in, in the browser (for a TV, on the phone they sign in with).
signIn.ownFirst: Turn on two-step sign-in for your own account first, in Account.
signIn.everyoneHasIt: Everyone with a password uses it already.
signIn.signsOut_one: Saving signs out {{count, number}} person who hasn't set it up, on every device and app, until they set it up.
signIn.signsOut_other: Saving signs out {{count, number}} people who haven't set it up, on every device and app, until they set it up.
signIn.noSecretKey: The server can't use its secret.key, so authenticator apps can't be set up or checked. Until it can, people who haven't set up two-step sign-in can't sign in, and people who have sign in with a recovery code. Its log says why.

apps.title: Apps
apps.thirdPartyHint: Pley's own apps can always sign in. Turn this on to let people allow other publishers' apps; turning it off signs them out.

watchingHours.mayBegin: The rest of the libraries may begin

transcoder.title: Transcoder
transcoder.description: Converts video a player can't play directly. Changes apply to new transcodes.
transcoder.managed: Started by Pley on this computer.

folder.label: Transcode folder
folder.hint: Holds stream segments, converted downloads and caches. Use a fast local disk with free space. If it can't be used, Pley falls back to the data folder.
folder.savedNextStart: Saved: Pley uses it from its next start
folder.problem: <folder>{{folder}}</folder> couldn't be used ({{reason}}), so the default folder is. Pley tries it again when it next starts.
folder.fixed: Chosen on Pley's command line or in its environment (PLEY_TRANSCODE_DIR).

video.title: Video
video.description: How video is encoded, decoded and tone mapped.
video.softwareInstead: {{reason}}: transcodes are encoded in software instead.
video.decodingHint: Decode on the GPU when possible.
video.decodedOnCpu: {{reason}}: videos are decoded on the CPU.
video.vulkanAlwaysOn: Always on with Vulkan, which decodes on the GPU.
video.vulkanNeedsIt: Vulkan needs it: transcodes are encoded in software instead.
video.presetHint: Faster presets use less CPU but make larger files (libx264 and libx265). Automatic adjusts to the computer's load.
video.tonemapHint: Convert HDR10, HLG and Dolby Vision to SDR when transcoding.
video.dolbyVisionNeeds: Dolby Vision needs an FFmpeg with libplacebo, and a GPU it reaches through Vulkan: <builds/>. Point Pley at it with --ffmpeg and --ffprobe, or in pley.toml.
video.tonemapWithAnother: {{reason}}: transcodes tone map with another instead.

builds.any: <gyan>gyan.dev's full build</gyan> on Windows, <jellyfin>jellyfin-ffmpeg</jellyfin> on Windows and Linux, or Homebrew's ffmpeg-full on a Mac

load.title: Load
load.description: How many transcodes run at once, and how far ahead of the player they work.
load.maxJobsManaged: The transcoder itself runs {{max}} at most (transcoder_max_jobs in pley.toml).
load.maxJobsExternal: The transcoder itself runs {{max}} at most (its --max-jobs).
load.throttleHint: Once a buffer is built, convert at real time. Saves CPU, GPU and disk for other playbacks.
load.noThrottling: This FFmpeg can't hold transcodes back: it needs FFmpeg 6.1 or newer.
load.memoryHint: Keeps segments in RAM instead of on disk.
load.memoryHintUpTo: Keeps segments in RAM instead of on disk. Up to {{size}}.

accelNeeds.vaapi: needs an Intel or AMD graphics chip

tonemapNeeds.libplacebo: needs libplacebo and a Vulkan GPU

choices.noGpuDecoder: no graphics card here that FFmpeg decodes on
choices.fitLibplaceboOnly: Set to Automatic: {{accel}} tone maps with libplacebo only.
choices.fitUnreached: Set to Automatic: {{tonemap}} doesn't reach {{accel}} here.
choices.fitDecoding: Turned on: {{accel}} decodes on the GPU.
choices.presetHevc: {{name}} encodes H.264 here: this applies to HEVC, and when software encodes instead.
choices.presetHdr: {{name}} encodes here: this applies to transcodes that keep HDR, and when software encodes instead.
choices.presetSoftware: {{name}} encodes here: this applies only when software encodes instead.
choices.tonemappedWith: HDR is tone mapped with {{name}} instead.
choices.noTonemapper: No tone mapper works here, so HDR may look washed out.

network.title: Network
network.description: Where Pley listens for browsers and apps. Changes apply at once, and Pley keeps them in <file>{{file}}</file>.

local.label: Only this computer
local.hint: For a reverse proxy on this computer that serves Pley with HTTPS (Caddy, nginx, IIS), or for Pley on its own.

networks.label: This computer and the networks chosen
networks.hint: Devices on those networks reach Pley at this computer's address there.

all.label: Every network
all.hint: Those that come later too: another Wi-Fi, a VPN.

jellyfin.hint: For Jellyfin apps such as Infuse.
jellyfin.portRange: The Jellyfin-compatible API's port is a number from 1 to 65535.
jellyfin.samePort: Choose another port for the Jellyfin-compatible API, or Pley's port.

plex.hint: For tools such as Kometa and Tautulli.
plex.portRange: The Plex-compatible API's port is a number from 1 to 65535.
plex.samePort: Choose another port for the Plex-compatible API, or Pley's port.

network.ownPort: On a port of its own

problems.port: The port is a number from 1 to 65535.
problems.sharedPort: The Jellyfin-compatible and Plex-compatible APIs can't share a port.
problems.noNetwork: Choose a network, or Only this computer.
problems.hostName: Bonjour's host name is letters, digits and hyphens, 63 at most, not starting or ending with a hyphen.

adapters.label: Networks
adapters.elsewhere: Not on this computer now: Pley listens there once it is.

network.fixedBind: Set by --bind or PLEY_BIND, on the command line or in the environment: change it there.
network.firewall: Windows Firewall decides which kinds of network reach Pley: Pley's Setup lets it through on private and domain networks, unless you chose otherwise there (run Setup again to change that).
network.portHint: The web app's and the Pley apps'.
network.localOnly: On networks only: devices can't reach this computer's own address.
network.containerNetwork: Pley runs on Docker's own network, where devices on yours can't find it: they need its address. Host networking, or br0 on Unraid, puts Pley on your network.

discovery.label: Found by the Pley apps
discovery.hint: The Pley apps on these networks find this server by themselves.

bonjour.label: Found by Apple's devices (Bonjour)
bonjour.fixed: Turned off by --no-bonjour, --no-discovery, PLEY_NO_BONJOUR or PLEY_NO_DISCOVERY.
bonjour.hint: Off unless turned on. Apple's devices find this server by it; without it, they need its address.
bonjour.hostNameHint: Where Apple's devices reach Pley; {{host}}.local when left empty. They list it by the server's name (Settings → Server).
bonjour.announcedOnHint: With a VPN, a virtual machine's or container's network, or a guest Wi-Fi, choose the networks whose devices should find Pley. Each network is told only Pley's address on it.
bonjour.everyHint: Those that come later too. 100.64.x.x ones (Tailscale) only when chosen.
bonjour.elsewhere: Not a network Pley listens on now: announced there once it is.

listening.title: Listening now
listening.retries: Pley retries addresses it can't listen on yet every 30 seconds.

network.unusual: Pley listens on {{addresses}}, which this page shows as near as it can: saving replaces them.
network.savedWaiting: Saved: Pley listens on the rest once it can
network.wouldStop: Pley would stop listening where this page is: it would stop working here.
network.pageMoves: This page moves to the new port.

proxy.title: Reached through a reverse proxy
proxy.description: Some proxies pass the address on without its port (nginx's $host, Nginx Proxy Manager). Pley then names itself without the port, and apps refuse it. Add the addresses with a port Pley is reached at that way, or have the proxy pass the port (proxy_set_header Host $http_host;).
proxy.openedAt: You opened Pley at <address>{{here}}</address>, but it is told <address>{{seen}}</address>: apps can't sign in at this address.

libraries.title: Libraries
libraries.description: Folders Pley watches for movies, shows and music.
libraries.sharedOrder: Everyone sees them in this order, unless they sort their own.
libraries.labelsPending: Waiting for Plex's labels: profiles with labels they never see don't see this library until an import that brings it finishes.
libraries.emptyDescription: Choose a type and the folders that contain your media. Pley scans them and keeps them up to date.
libraries.deleteMessage: <name>{{name}}</name> and its watch history will be removed from Pley. Your media files are not touched.

form.name: Name
form.nothingMounted: Pley runs in a container, and no media folder is mounted into it yet. Mount yours at <path>/media</path> (with Docker, <path>-v /your/media:/media:ro</path>), then restart the container.

users.title: Users
users.description: Who can sign in, what each person can see, and the profiles of your home.
users.deleteMessage: <name>{{name}}</name> will lose access, and their watch history and settings will be deleted.

twoStep.title: Two-step sign-in
twoStep.hint: Signs in with a code from an authenticator app after the password.
twoStep.hintRequired: Signs in with a code from an authenticator app after the password. Turning it off signs {{name}} out everywhere, to set it up again at the next sign-in.
twoStep.turnOffTitle: For someone who lost their phone and their recovery codes
twoStep.signedOut: {{name}} is signed out, and sets up two-step sign-in again at the next sign-in

dialog.regularText: Signs in with a username and password.
dialog.managedText: No password: a child or guest you switch to from your profile.
dialog.usernameManagedHint: Only used internally for managed profiles.
dialog.displayNameHint: Shown in the profile switcher and menus.
dialog.ownPassword: Your own password, PIN and two-step sign-in change in Account, which asks for your current password.
dialog.managedPasswordHint: Setting one turns this profile into a regular account.
dialog.noPasswordHint: This account has no password: set one so it can sign in.
dialog.keepPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the current one.
dialog.adminHint: Can manage libraries, users and server settings.
dialog.homeHint: Shown in the profile switcher, so household members can switch to each other.
dialog.disabledHint: Can't sign in or play anything until enabled again.
dialog.requestsAdmin: Administrators' requests are approved as they make them.
dialog.requestsAgeLimit: Asking for movies and shows in Discover, which leaves out titles above the age limit.
dialog.requestsHint: Asking for movies and shows the libraries don't have, in Discover.
dialog.requestAsk: May ask, for an administrator to approve
dialog.pinSet: This profile has a PIN. Enter a new one to change it.
dialog.pinHint: Optional, 4 to 8 digits. Needed to switch to this profile.
dialog.pinDigits: The PIN must be 4 to 8 digits.
dialog.pickLibrary: Pick at least one library, or allow all of them.

invites.title: Invitations
invites.description: Share your libraries with friends: each link lets people create their own account.
invites.emptyDescription: Create a link and send it to someone. You choose which libraries they can see and an optional age limit.
invites.deleteMessage: The link stops working. Accounts already created with it are kept.

create.intro: Anyone with the link can create their own account. They join as friends of this server (not home members) with the access you choose here.
create.noteHint: Only you see it, e.g. who the link is for.
create.pickLibrary: Pick at least one library, or share all of them.
create.atLeastOne: The link must allow at least one sign-up.

ready.title: Invitation ready
ready.send: Send this link to the person you're inviting:

requests.title: Requests
requests.unsupportedHint: Update Pley to let people ask for movies and shows.
requests.description: People ask for movies and shows the libraries don't have, found on TMDB. You approve or decline each.
requests.takeHint: Discover and Requests show in the menu of every account that may ask.
requests.needsTmdb: Needs a TMDB API key: add one in Server.
requests.moviesHint: How many each account may ask for in any 7 days. Administrators have no limit.
requests.whoMayAsk: Who may ask, and whose requests are approved as they're made, is up to each account in Users. Administrators' are always approved.

arr.radarr: Movies approved are added to Radarr, which finds and downloads them.
arr.sonarr: Shows approved are added to Sonarr with the seasons asked for, which it finds and downloads.
arr.connectToChoose: Connect to choose a quality profile and a folder.
arr.addressHint: Where Pley reaches {{name}}, as {{example}}. Empty: what's approved is added by hand.
arr.forgetsKey: Saving without an address forgets the API key too.
arr.typeKey: Type {{name}}'s API key for this address: the saved one goes only to the address it was saved with.
arr.approvingFails: Approving fails until one is chosen.
arr.minimumAvailabilityHint: When Radarr may take a release of a movie asked for.
arr.animeProfileHint: For titles TMDB counts as anime.
arr.seasonFoldersHint: A folder for each season of a show.
arr.searchMovie: Look for the movie as soon as it's approved.
arr.searchSeasons: Look for the seasons asked for as soon as they're approved.

dashboard.title: Dashboard

gpu.label: GPU
gpu.title: Decoded, filtered and encoded on the GPU without copies

waits.busy: waits while other programs keep the processors busy
waits.scanning: waits while new libraries are scanned or imported
waits.auto: what's likely to be watched soon first, the rest in quieter hours
waits.autoFrom: what's likely to be watched soon first, the rest in quieter hours (from {{time}})

dashboard.nobodyWatching: Nobody is watching anything right now.
dashboard.nothingPlayed: Nothing has been played to the end yet.

resources.title: Resources
resources.pleyHint: The server, its transcoder and their FFmpegs
resources.couldntRead: Couldn't read the processors and memory: {{error}}
resources.unmeasurable: The processors and memory can't be measured on this system.

storage.title: Storage
storage.damagedHint: {{problem}}. Stop Pley, move pley.db and its -wal and -shm files aside, and copy the latest backup in their place.

signIn.title: Sign in with Plex
signIn.description: Pley reads your Plex server through Plex's own sign-in. It sees what you allow and keeps nothing once the import is over.
signIn.expired: Plex's sign-in page has expired. Sign in again.
signIn.tokenHint: For a server you sign in to another way. Pley forgets it with the rest of the sign-in.

server.title: Which server?
server.description: The Plex servers your account owns.
server.none: This Plex account doesn't own a Plex server. Sign in with the account that owns yours.
server.sharedOnly: The Plex servers this account can open belong to someone else ({{servers}}). Only the account that owns a server can bring everyone's watch history and the Home's restrictions over, so sign in with that one. On Plex's page, switch to it first if Plex signs you straight in.
server.addressHint: When Pley can't reach your server at the addresses Plex gives.

plan.couldntRead: Pley couldn't read your Plex server

libraries.title: Libraries on {{server}}
libraries.none: This server has no movie, show or music libraries.
libraries.plexSees: Plex sees <path>{{folder}}</path>. Where does Pley see it?
libraries.unsureHint: Some of its files aren't in this library, so what Plex knows of them won't come over.

problem.no_folders: Say where at least one of its folders is for Pley.

libraries.pickOne: Choose at least one library to bring.

check.none_found: None of Plex's files are here

people.title: Who comes over
people.description: Each person in your Plex Home becomes a profile, with what they watched and the limits Plex set for them.
people.found: Their profile from an earlier import
people.leftOver_one: A profile keeps 50 labels of up to 120 characters; this one is left out: {{labels}}
people.leftOver_other: A profile keeps 50 labels of up to 120 characters; these are left out: {{labels}}
people.notKept: Pley can't keep these rules of Plex's, so it hides more instead:
people.pinHint: If Plex asks for it. Pley doesn't keep it.

bring.title: What to bring
bring.description: Libraries and people come over whatever you choose. Turn off what you'd rather start over in Pley.
bring.watchHistoryHint: Watched titles, resume points, ratings and every play.
bring.collectionsHint: Collections in their order, with their labels, and each person's playlists. Smart ones stay behind.
bring.editsHint: Titles matched as Plex has them, and fields edited in Plex as edits in Pley. Kometa locks the fields it sets, so its changes come too.

progress.title: Importing from Plex
progress.description: This can take a while on a big server. You can close this and come back: it goes on.

steps.matching_again: Finding the rest of Plex's titles

progress.stopMessage: What's already come over stays. Pley also forgets your Plex sign-in, so importing again starts by signing in.
progress.inDescription: What everyone watched is in Pley. It's fetching posters and details, then looking for the rest of Plex's titles. You can start watching now: the report will be under Import from Plex in Settings › Libraries.

report.done: Your Plex library is in Pley
report.lostHint: Pley restarted while it ran, so there's no report. What came over before stays; importing again brings the rest and nothing twice. Settings › Libraries marks libraries still waiting for Plex's labels.
report.doneHint: Here's what came over. Importing again later brings what's new and nothing twice.
report.partHint: What came over before it stopped stays. Importing again brings the rest and nothing twice.

skipped.pin_needed: Not brought: Plex asked for their PIN.
skipped.refused: Not brought: Plex didn't let Pley in as them.
skipped.no_access: Not brought: they can't open this Plex server.

report.incomplete: Plex refused some of their lists, so some of what they watched didn't come over.
report.playlistsIncomplete: Plex refused some of their playlists, so not all of them came over.
report.notKept: Rules Pley couldn't keep, so it hides more instead:
report.notKeptOwnLimit: Rules Pley couldn't keep; the profile keeps the age limit it has in Pley:
report.closed_one: {{libraries}} stays closed to this profile: it holds more than Plex shared with them. You can open it in Settings › Users.
report.closed_other: {{libraries}} stay closed to this profile: they hold more than Plex shared with them. You can open them in Settings › Users.
report.labelsPending: Still waiting for Plex's labels, so profiles with labels they never see don't see it. Importing this library again brings them, or you can show it now in Settings › Libraries.
report.missedUnlabelled: Titles Pley couldn't find don't have Plex's labels, so the labels this profile never sees don't hide them.
report.matchesFixed_one: {{count, number}} title matched as in Plex
report.matchesFixed_other: {{count, number}} titles matched as in Plex
report.smartLeft_one: {{count, number}} smart collection or playlist left behind
report.smartLeft_other: {{count, number}} smart collections and playlists left behind
report.editsHint: Tools such as Kometa lock the fields they set, so a field edited on most titles is likely theirs.

status.fillingIn: Titles fill in with their details and posters as Pley fetches them.
status.cancelled: The Plex import was stopped on {{date}}
status.interrupted: The Plex import started on {{date}} was cut short when Pley restarted
